sermon.title: Six Irrational Beliefs
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer shows six irrational New Testament beliefs—the Sadducees, the Pharisees, the resurrection already past, circumcision for salvation, marriage in heaven, and a natural kingdom—then six questionable doctrines today: the imminent return, a pre-tribulation rapture, staying out of politics, all religions leading to God, America in prophecy, and faith alone. We are saved by his love unto good works.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: One word at 4:30 was not clear. Caption fixes: Hymenaeus and Philetus, Ananias, Oprah Winfrey and Joel Osteen (named as teaching all religions lead to God). He cites Matthew 22:9 for the Sadducees’ question (22:23–30), attributes hastening the Lord’s coming to Paul (2 Peter 3:12) and “through much tribulation” to Jesus (Acts 14:22, Paul and Barnabas). Unchecked: 60–70% of Israel atheist. Doctrinal positions kept as spoken: once saved always saved bogus, baptism washes away sins, not faith alone, no pre-tribulation rapture, US not in prophecy.

chunks.section_question: Must you be circumcised to be saved?

Ananias told Paul to be baptized and wash away his sins (Acts 22:16), and Acts 2 calls for repentance in Jesus’ name for remission of sins and the Holy Spirit.

faqs.question: Who were the Sadducees?
faqs.answer: A religious group of the Jews the high priest came from; they said there is no resurrection, angel or spirit.

faqs.question: Is once saved always saved true?
faqs.answer: He says 2 Timothy 2:17 shows it is bogus—you can’t stray from something you weren’t with.

faqs.question: What was circumcision a shadow of?
faqs.answer: Water baptism, used of God to cleanse you from your sin.

faqs.question: Is there reincarnation?
faqs.answer: No—it is appointed to man once to die and after death the judgment.

faqs.question: Can Christians eat shrimp, catfish or pork?
faqs.answer: Yes—the diet was an illustration of righteousness, a shadow law we don’t keep now.

faqs.question: Can we hasten the Lord’s coming?
faqs.answer: He says yes, by righteousness—there is a move of God coming where the church lives as a light.

faqs.question: Will natural Israel come to Christ?
faqs.answer: He says God will visit natural Israel and graft them back in to Jesus.

faqs.question: Should Christians avoid government?
faqs.answer: No—it would be wise to have righteous leaders rather than corrupt ones.

faqs.question: What do good works do?
faqs.answer: They keep families healthy and make communities and nations strong, and bring honor to your Father in heaven.

faqs.question: Does God give up on people?
faqs.answer: No—he remains faithful and keeps working to win you to himself until the day you die.
